properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Cabarrus County in the piedmont of North
Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 1215 AM EDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.  A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 609 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
torrential rain due to a stationary thunderstorm south of Mount
Pleasant and east of Harrisburg near Midland. Between 1 and 2
inches of rain have fallen so far, but an additional inch or more
of rainfall is possible before the causative thunderstorm weakens
or drifts away from the area. Given wet antecedent conditions
across southern Cabarrus County from multiple rounds of
thunderstorms over the past week, excessive runoff is likely to
cause rapid small stream rises and areas of adjacent lowland
flooding.  Poorly draining intersections and low spots along
roadways are likely to flood.  Exercise caution when encountering
ponding and avoid flooded roadways.  Areas of greatest concern
include along Reedy Creek near Lower Rocky River Rd, Anderson
Creek near Bethel Church Rd, Horton Branch near Robert Bost Rd,
and Caldwell Creek near Rebel Dr.

Additional showers are developing over Harrisburg.  While the
rainfall over Harrisburg has not been significant enough yet
to cause excessive runoff, the slow-moving nature of this
line of storms may result in excessive runoff within the next
60 minutes.  Therefore, the Flood Advisory will extend
upstream within the Rocky River watershed across the southern
third of Cabarrus County.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Harrisburg, Mt Pleasant, and Midland.
